## 408. Which class P2 reads, and how what one leaves out is divided (OC1)

PF2 left 07 §4.6 one question, raised in the IV3 line's review of its edits ([note](../../development/iv3-dependence/REVIEW-PF2.md)). Constancy up to the net's end constrains every block of a class, what lies outside a self's class included. So which class P2 should read, and how finely that class divides what one leaves out, fixes how much P2 asks. OC1 answers it in `Becoming.GrammarPath`, below PF's and PF2's laws (board rule 9): their statements stay, and their proofs now go through the forms at a member's class.

**What it says.** The path never used more than the self's own class: each of its laws compares only occurrences alike to the member. Over the whole class, constancy up to the net's end asks the same of every block of what lies outside, and it can fail for reasons that are not the self's (`UnevenOutside`). Read at one's own class, P2 still excludes the organism. The division of what one leaves out matters only to a self that does not hold its effects. Under the split of oneself from the rest, which asks least, P2 asks of such a self only this: where any occurrence alike to it conditions something inside, every alike occurrence that goes on does, and where any conditions something outside, every one that goes on does. So P2 passes a self drawn by intention wherever every occurrence alike to it that goes on both conditions something inside and leaves something outside, and the crux is P4. PF2 argued this from one witness; it now holds as a law.

**Constructivity.** No omniscience principle. The split is given by a decided predicate, and the cases are distinguished on `Bool` (`decEq`). The receipt's empty axiom reports are the evidence.
